title: introduce idempotent db-migrate hook and secret-drift-reconcile post-upgrade job
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Private installs running in air-gapped / VPC environments require deterministic and safe upgrades. Two recurring operator pain points: (1) ad-hoc DB migration jobs causing duplicate migrations on retries or during rollbacks, and (2) secret drift between chart values and KMS-backed secrets after upgrade. This PR adds two new Helm hooks and supporting helpers: an idempotent-db-migrate Job (pre-upgrade, pre-install) that uses a lightweight lease + migration-state ConfigMap to make migrations safe to re-run, and a post-upgrade secret-drift-reconcile Job that reconciles values.yaml secret equivalents with KMS/HSM-backed Kubernetes Secrets, performing an atomic rotate/re-encrypt when drift is detected.

Design/changes in this PR: - templates/hooks/idempotent-db-migrate-job.yaml: new pre-install, pre-upgrade hook implementing a leader-less lease pattern and marking progress in a namespaced ConfigMap so the job is safe across retries. It supports a --dry-run flag used during canaries. - templates/hooks/secret-drift-reconcile-job.yaml: post-upgrade hook that calls into the same auth path used by the private-installer to fetch KMS-wrapped secrets; it supports a fallback no-op mode when KMS is not configured. - templates/_helpers.tpl: new helper functions tenancy.overlay and install.preflight.network-check used by the templates to keep tenancy overlays small and make preflight checks reusable. - values.schema.json: extended schema with migration.enabled/migration.image/migration.timeout and secrets.reconcile.enabled/kms.provider/kms.path fields and validation. - README-PRIVATE.md: documented operator workflow for upgrades, including how to toggle --force-run-migrations and how to observe migration progress via the migration ConfigMap. - Chart.yaml: chart version bump and note about Helm v3.9 compatibility. - examples/terraform-private-module/README.md: brief note on Terraform module variables that should be provided when enabling reconcile and KMS-based secrets.

Testing: - Unit-tested helper templates with helm template against a matrix of values (single-tenant vs multi-tenant). - Integration: deployed to a private staging cluster with KMS stub and exercised: fresh install, upgrade with schema change, simulated failed migration (job exit code 1) followed by retry to verify idempotency, and simulated secret drift to verify reconcile path. - CI: initial linting caught strict schema violations; fixed and re-ran; CI pipeline passed full chart lint + kubeval + minimal rendering tests. - Observability: added a migration_progress metric emitted as an annotation on the migration ConfigMap; the post-upgrade job emits a reconcile_summary event to cluster Event API.

Rollout plan: - Canary on internal private clusters for 48 hours (feature gated by values.migration.enabled and values.secrets.reconcile.enabled default off). - Once stable, flip migration.enabled by default in the next minor release after operator/installer teams validate the Terraform integration.

Rollback safety: The idempotent migration writes a handshake key into the migration ConfigMap only after each migration step succeeds; on rollback the job inspects the ConfigMap and will not reapply already-applied steps. The secret-drift job is a post-upgrade hook and runs only after resources are updated; it performs a preflight dry-run and writes to a staging Secret first, then atomically swaps with the live secret using a kubernetes patch call so we can revert by restoring the staging secret if needed.
commits: 9f2a3c4: add idempotent-db-migrate job, helper templates, and migration ConfigMap semantics
2b7d1e9: add secret-drift-reconcile post-upgrade job with KMS fallback and tests
c4187a0: values.schema.json extended and README-PRIVATE.md upgrade notes
d5e6f12: examples: document terraform variables and bump chart version
changed_files:
templates/hooks/idempotent-db-migrate-job.yaml: |
  apiVersion: batch/v1
  kind: Job
  metadata:
    name: {{ include "redwood.fullname" . }}-db-migrate
    annotations:
      helm.sh/hook: pre-upgrade,pre-install
      helm.sh/hook-weight: "0"

templates/hooks/secret-drift-reconcile-job.yaml: |
  apiVersion: batch/v1
  kind: Job
  metadata:
    name: {{ include "redwood.fullname" . }}-secret-reconcile
    annotations:
      helm.sh/hook: post-upgrade
      helm.sh/hook-delete-policy: hook-succeeded

README-PRIVATE.md: |
  ## Upgrade notes
  - To enable idempotent migrations set `migration.enabled` to true and provide a migration.image.
  - Use `helm upgrade --wait` to surface migration failures to the caller.

Chart.yaml: |
  apiVersion: v2
  name: redwood-private
  version: 1.14.0
  deprecated: false
examples/terraform-private-module/README.md: |\n  When enabling secret reconciliation, provide `kms_provider` and `kms_path` via the module inputs.

release_notes: Add idempotent pre-install/pre-upgrade DB migrations and a post-upgrade secret reconciliation job for KMS-backed secrets. Both features are opt-in via values.migration.enabled and values.secrets.reconcile.enabled. No breaking changes.
notes_for_ops: Feature-gated off by default. When enabling on private clusters ensure installer has KMS access and RBAC rights to read/write migration ConfigMaps and patch/seal Secrets.
testing_matrix: helm lint + kubeval + helm template matrix (single-tenant, multi-tenant) + staging integration with KMS stub; simulated failure + retry scenarios covered.
